chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
the testimony of a woman who was present with a man making a bequest, with no other man with her. So he said: A quarter of what was bequeathed is permitted, in proportion to her testimony.

key_terms.بِحِسَاب: By reckoning/proportion; indicating a calculated proportional allowance
key_terms.رُبُع: One quarter; the fraction recognized as proportionate to one woman's testimony in this jurisprudential ruling
key_terms.شَهَادَة: Testimony, witness; the legal act of giving witness in a court or legal setting
key_terms.يُوصِي: Making a bequest; the act of bequeathing property or instructions before death (wasiyya)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's testimony in bequest cases according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that when a woman is the sole witness to a man's bequest (dying will), only one quarter of what was bequeathed is enforceable — reflecting the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that one female witness carries one-quarter of the evidentiary weight of two male witnesses (two men being full testimony). This ruling falls within the broader Shia fiqh framework on testimonial proportionality in inheritance and wills, where female testimony is accepted but its legal effect is proportionally scaled according to classical jurisprudential standards.
